info.title: EH3D Server API
info.summary: The REST and websocket interface of the EH3D server.
info.description: Everything is under `/api/v1/` and answers JSON. A mistake is `{"error": "<code>", "detail": "..."}` with the status that fits; the codes are the catalog in `docs/error-codes.json`. Except the health check, the first set-up and the login, every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: the token of a login or the token of a program. A viewer reads, an operator also prepares, starts, stops and confirms jobs, an administrator also manages users, tokens and machines; a token may be limited further by scopes. Limits: passwords are 8 to 128 characters, a request body is at most `max_body_mb` of `server.cfg` (else `too_big`), a ticket is good for one use within 30 seconds, and five wrong passwords block a name for a while (`throttled`). `docs/API.md` explains the behaviour; this document is the contract of the routes.

servers.description: The default port of the server is 18200.

get.summary: Health check

post.description: Needs the set-up code the server prints on its console. With `local_until_setup` on, only the computer the server runs on may call it while there is no user. No login.

post.summary: Log in
post.description: Five wrong passwords block the name for a while. The login survives a restart only with `persist_sessions`. No login.

put.description: A token of a program has no password and is refused with `403 forbidden`. A person logged in (not a token).

post.summary: Make a ticket for the camera or the websocket
post.description: Good for one use within 30 seconds and made for the session that asked, so the address of the camera or of the websocket never carries the token. Any login or token.

get.summary: Open the websocket of the events
get.description: The first text is `hello` with the summaries of the jobs; then `job`, `job_removed`, `machine`, `task`, `task_removed`, `project`, `revision` and `project_removed`, the last four only for who may see them; `resync` tells a client that fell behind to ask again. The server pings every `events_ping_s` and closes idle connections. Role viewer or higher.

put.summary: Write a file as a new version
put.description: Never overwrites: every change of the bytes is a new version. A file that exists needs `If-Match` with the SHA-256 of the version the new bytes were made from (`428 precondition_required` without it, `412 precondition_failed` if it is not the current one); a new file takes none. Answers `201` for a new version and `200` when nothing changed. Role operator or higher. Scope `projects:write` if the token is limited by scopes.

get.summary: List the catalogs
get.description: Every catalog with its version, its number of items and its tag, also the ones nobody uploaded to. Role viewer or higher. Scope `catalog:read` if the token is limited by scopes.

get.summary: Search a catalog
get.description: With the `ETag` of the dataset in the header (its content, so it changes only when the dataset does). A client that keeps a copy sends it back in `If-None-Match`. Role viewer or higher. Scope `catalog:read` if the token is limited by scopes.

parameters.name: catalog
parameters.description: The name of a catalog (`materials`, `tools`, `machine-profiles`, `footprints`, `symbols` or `components`).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Keep the items that have this text in any value, in any letter case.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Conditions `field:value` separated by commas: the field (`a.b` for a nested one) equals the value in any letter case; a value that starts with `~` only has to contain the rest; on a list one of the values has to match.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by (numbers as numbers, the rest as text).

parameters.name: desc
parameters.description: Descending.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page (50, at most `catalog_page_max`).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Items to skip.

304.description: The `If-None-Match` tag is the one of the catalog: nothing changed. No body.

put.summary: Replace the dataset of a catalog
put.description: The whole dataset, as a new version, or nothing: one item that does not fit refuses the upload. The built-in `materials` is not written. Audited and told on the stream as `catalog.changed`. Role admin. Scope `catalog:write` if the token is limited by scopes.

parameters.name: catalog
parameters.description: The name of a catalog (`materials`, `tools`, `machine-profiles`, `footprints`, `symbols` or `components`).

delete.description: A new version with no items; the file of the previous one stays beside it. Role admin. Scope `catalog:write` if the token is limited by scopes.

parameters.name: catalog
parameters.description: The name of a catalog (`materials`, `tools`, `machine-profiles`, `footprints`, `symbols` or `components`).

get.summary: Read one item of a catalog
get.description: Role viewer or higher. Scope `catalog:read` if the token is limited by scopes.

parameters.name: catalog
parameters.description: The name of a catalog (`materials`, `tools`, `machine-profiles`, `footprints`, `symbols` or `components`).

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The name of an item of the catalog (the value of its `id`, or of its `name` for footprints and symbols).

bearerAuth.description: The token of a login (`POST /login`) or of a program (`POST /tokens`).

ticketAuth.name: ticket
ticketAuth.description: A ticket from `POST /tickets`, for the camera and the websocket.

detail.description: Words for a person; may be empty.

ErrorBody.description: Every refusal has this shape, with the status that fits the code.

Health.description: `uptime_s`, `storage`, `recovered_locks` and `features` come only with a valid token.

code.description: The set-up code the server prints on its console.

Token.description: Seconds since 1970 for `created`, `last_used` and `expires`; the secret is never listed.

scopes.description: Scopes that narrow the role, see the scopes table of docs/API.md.

token.description: The node's access token; never shown by the API (`token_set` instead), and empty on an update keeps the stored one.

port.description: Serial port of a GRBL controller.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 32.

station.description: The bench, room or workshop; empty when none.

cfg.description: The tuning text of the machine; keys that hold secrets are shown empty.

RackSlot.description: The place of the rack one tool of the job is in.

first.description: How many places of the rack the tools of the jobs before this one take (0 for the first job of the load).

carry_in.description: The chuck comes holding the last tool of the job before: the first change takes it to its place and picks the first tool of this job.

carry_out.description: This job leaves its last tool in the chuck for the next one.

slots.description: The place of each tool of this job; a tool that is not listed is taken from the place the order of the job gives it.

carry_slot.description: With `carry_in`, the place of the tool the chuck comes holding.

JobRackV2.description: The chaining of the tool changer of a request of the second version. Every field is optional; a field this server does not know is left out and named in a warning. See docs/ATC_CHAIN.md.

request_version.description: `2` when `rack` is present; absent in the requests of the first version.

DrillRequest.description: The holes or the files, not both (`both_sources`).

request_version.description: `2` when `rack` is present; absent in the requests of the first version.

RouteRequest.description: The paths or the files, not both (`both_sources`).

gcode.description: The text of the program; at most a million lines.

rack_applied.description: Only when the request had a `rack`: `true` when the plan used it, `false` when it was left out (a `rack_*` warning says why).

JobView.description: What a client draws and follows; see `The view` in docs/API.md.

rack_applied.description: As in the view: present only when the request had a `rack`.

JobResponse.description: The answer to a request for a job. With a `rack` in the request, `rack_applied` is `true` when the server planned with it, and `view.warnings` lists what was left out (`rack_needs_v2`, `rack_no_changer`, `rack_unknown_field`, `request_version_newer`).

NodeAnswer.description: The node's own answer, with its own status code.

InspectProfile.description: `px_per_mm`, which checks are on and every tolerance; `preset` (`standard`, `fine_pitch` or `prototype`) starts from a preset.

project.description: The id of the artifact the task works on.

name.description: 1 to 120 characters, no control characters or slashes.

format.description: A media type in lower case.

UploadComplete.description: The description of an artifact, as in `POST /artifacts` without the bytes.

Project.description: `shares` only for the owner and the administrators.

parent.description: The revision this one follows; 0 for the first.

NewShare.description: A user or a token, not both.

StoreFile.description: The current version of a file of a project.

StoreLock.description: Who is editing the project and until when (seconds since 1970).

StoreVersion.description: One version of a file: its number, the SHA-256 of its bytes (also its tag) and who wrote it.

StoreWriteResult.description: The version written; `unchanged` is true when the bytes were those of the current version and no version was made.

CatalogSummary.description: `version` is 0 for a catalog nobody uploaded to; `source` is `embedded`, `json` or `csv`.

CatalogItem.description: One item, as the dataset has it; the field that names it is `id` (`name` for footprints and symbols).

CatalogDataset.description: A list of items, or an object with the list under `tools`, `profiles`, `footprints`, `symbols` or `parts` (`items` also works); the components base declares `"format": "phoenix-parts/1"`. As CSV (`Content-Type: text/csv`): a header line and a row per item, the values as text.
